clue.text: Once more performing without little Maureen? Yes

definitions.text: Once more performing without little Maureen? Yes

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters of the words once more are put through their paces into a new order
without says some letters of the pool are left out of the rearrangement

parts.note: Mo is a short, pet form of the name Maureen

explanation.surface: An audience cheers for a singer to come back on, even without the diminutive Maureen; yes, please.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of ONCE MORE, drop M and O (little Maureen), and 'performing' rearranges the rest. The whole clue doubles as the audience's call for a repeat performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A call for a performer to give a repeated item, which is what the audience shouts when they want once more.

clue.text: The remainder of last month

indicators.note: the remainder is what is left of the month's name once its usual short form is taken away

parts.note: December is the final month of the year

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is left over from the previous month.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove DEC, the standard abbreviation of the month, from DECEMBER and the remainder is the answer; that answer is itself a remainder, the glowing bit left of a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing fragment left in a dying fire is a remnant, what remains after the blaze.

clue.text: Players don't want this at 6, 20 from jazz fan

indicators.note: from says the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
20 across is the second word of the linked answer at 6, meaning appeal

explanation.surface: A jazz fan heckles at the end of the show, something actors dread at their bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 and 20 together are CURTAIN CALL, the moment the cast returns to bow; the 20 part on its own supplies the second half of this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeering whistle from the audience is the last thing a cast hopes to hear when taking a bow.

clue.text: Take another look at limit on first pupil in group

parts.note: to rein in is to limit, and a rein is a restraint

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the word for a group

parts.note: a sect is a group, typically religious

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word pupil

parts.note: only its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A teacher reviewing a class decides how far to restrict the first pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' tempts as the definition of a schoolchild, but only its opening letter is used, tucked in by 'in'; 'on' just joins the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something again is to look at it a second time, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: One's friends move around seated area

definitions.meaning: a social set, the people one mixes with
to go round something, as a bird of prey does overhead
the dress or upper tier of seats in a theatre

explanation.surface: A person and their pals shuffle about looking for somewhere to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: a social set, to orbit, and an upper tier of theatre seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a social group, travelling round in a loop, and a balcony tier of theatre seating.

clue.text: Toughen up one sister, maybe, not second

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: not says the letter standing for second is left out

parts.note: a sister is a senior nurse in a British hospital, hence the maybe

explanation.surface: Advice to a nun or sibling to become more resilient, though not to come second.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a Sister is a senior nurse. Dropping S from NURSE leaves NURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To accustom someone to hardship so they become hardened to it is to toughen them.

clue.text: Summons to return for screen appeal

parts.note: a curtain is a screen, hung to hide something
a call is an appeal or request

explanation.surface: Phrased like a cinema's invitation to bring an attractive film back to the screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Applause summoning performers back onstage at the end of a show to take a bow.

clue.text: Uneven steps after team break

indicators.note: after places the steps letters behind the team

parts.note: a cricket or football side has eleven players

indicators.note: uneven picks the odd-numbered letters of the word steps, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A footballer's awkward strides after training as the side stops for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uneven' takes the odd letters of STEPS, giving SES. In Britain elevenses is a light snack and pause around eleven in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A mid-morning pause for tea or coffee and a biscuit, an everyday British rest from work.

clue.text: Keep away from type of blood spot

parts.note: AB is one of the human blood groups
a stain is a spot or mark

explanation.surface: A warning to avoid a bloodstain of a particular group.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from something, especially drink or a vote, is to hold back from it.

clue.text: Four playing to measure extra time

parts.note: a quart is a measure of liquid, two pints
ET is the abbreviation for extra time in football

explanation.surface: A football match that goes to extra time, four players measuring it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Four musicians performing together form a group of that size, as in a string ensemble.

clue.text: Legal ownership requires duty to lead

parts.note: title is the legal right to own property
a role is a job or function, a duty one performs

explanation.surface: A lawyer's maxim that owning property obliges one to take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The lead in a play or film is the part bearing the work's own name, as Hamlet is in Hamlet.

clue.text: Same 4 demolished cake

indicators.note: demolished means knocked down and rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: 4 across is the word meaning one's friends or a seated area

explanation.surface: The same friends from 4 wolfed down the cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demolished' plays on eating up a cake, but it rearranges SAME with CIRCLE, the answer at 4.
explanation.definitionFit: A layered pastry filled with cream, a British bakery treat often iced on top.

clue.text: Swear it'll be found in Faversham

indicators.note: it will be found in says the letters sit within the town name

explanation.surface: Someone vows that something can be found in the Kent town of Faversham.
explanation.walkthrough: Faversham is a market town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm or declare something firmly is to state it as on oath.

clue.text: Search for girl clutching meal ticket

indicators.note: clutching means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: Dee is a girl's name
LV stands for luncheon voucher, a meal ticket issued to British workers

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for a young woman who is grasping her lunch voucher.
explanation.walkthrough: A luncheon voucher (LV) was a paper ticket British employers gave staff to pay for lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig into something in pursuit of information is to research it deeply.

clue.text: Pinter, say, to start amid confusion

indicators.note: confusion means the letters of start and amid are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Harold Pinter is told to begin while chaos reigns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amid' looks like a link but is fodder, with 'confusion' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Pinter was a celebrated English playwright, an example of a writer for the stage.

clue.text: Scottish location famous for its adaptable mentors!

definitions.text: Scottish location famous for its adaptable mentors!

parts.words: Scottish location famous for its adaptable mentors!
parts.note: a rearrangeable word, mentors, can be juggled into the beast this Highland lake is famous for

explanation.surface: A Scottish place known for its flexible teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adaptable mentors' rearranges into MONSTER; the loch is famed for its legendary monster, Nessie.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep freshwater lake in the Scottish Highlands, home of the legendary Nessie.

clue.text: Storm after A-lister takes charge of ceremony

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun, one who leads a rite

indicators.note: after places the storm word behind the star

parts.note: an A-lister is a top celebrity, a celeb
to rant is to storm, raging loudly

explanation.surface: A star throws a tantrum and then runs the proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest or official who performs a religious rite or a wedding presides over it.

clue.text: Decay on Scottish island upset commentator

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: rot is decay
Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

explanation.surface: Rot on a Scottish island has upset a broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses ROTARRAN as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone giving a spoken account of events, like a voice-over, is a commentator.

clue.text: They made Robin dependent

definitions.meaning: a British car firm built the Robin, a three-wheeled car

explanation.surface: A company made Batman's sidekick reliant on others.
explanation.walkthrough: The Robin was a three-wheeled car made by the British firm of this name, not the comic-book Robin.
explanation.definitionFit: Trusting or leaning on others is being dependent; the name is also the British maker of the Robin car.

clue.text: Crocodiles' tracks

definitions.meaning: a crocodile is a column of schoolchildren walking in pairs

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'crocodile' is a file of schoolchildren walking two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: Files of walkers and railway tracks are both rows or routes; the plural noun fits each.

clue.text: Opening whereby crooked personality avoids PAYE

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
avoids means the letters of PAYE are kept out of the result

parts.note: Pay As You Earn, the British income tax system, read as its four letters

explanation.surface: A dishonest celebrity finds a loophole to dodge income tax.
explanation.walkthrough: PAYE (Pay As You Earn) is how British employees pay income tax. Take those four letters from PERSONALITY and 'crooked' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the two openings in the nose through which air is breathed.

clue.text: See 6
Go on and on speaking of young girl and boy

indicators.note: speaking of means the words are said out loud and matched by their sound

parts.note: a filly is a young girl, and Buster is a nickname for a boy

explanation.surface: Someone drones on while talking about a lass and lad.
explanation.walkthrough: FILLY + BUSTER said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstructing a vote by making very long speeches means talking interminably.

clue.text: Comedy at distant church

parts.note: far means distant
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A comic show performed at a remote church.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad comic play built on absurd situations is a type of comedy.

clue.text: It's 50/50 First Lady adopts new style

indicators.note: adopts means the first piece takes on the second, which follows it

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible
NS is the abbreviation for New Style, the Gregorian calendar dating

explanation.surface: A president's wife takes on a fresh look, with even odds of success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife but is EVE; 'new style' is the calendar abbreviation NS, dating by the Gregorian reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds of one to one in betting give an equal chance, a 50/50 shot.

clue.text: Artisan turned performer

indicators.note: turned means twisted around into another order

explanation.surface: A craftsman became an entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was a famous American singer and actor, an example of a performer.

clue.text: Conveyor belt to airline

definitions.meaning: anything that transports goods, a conveyor

explanation.surface: A baggage belt leading to an airline desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A transporting device and a passenger airline company are both things that convey.

clue.text: Gossip one time too many for society magazine

indicators.note: too many says one of the doubled letters is surplus and goes

parts.note: a tattler is a gossip, someone who tells tales
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Tittle-tattle once too often in a glossy for high society.
explanation.walkthrough: The gossip has one T too many; remove it.
explanation.definitionFit: The British glossy monthly covering upper-class social events and parties.

clue.text: Compartments are unlikely on board

indicators.note: on board here means aboard a vessel, so one piece sits inside the ship's letters

parts.note: to be on board is to be on a ship, abbreviated SS for steamship
tall means unlikely, as in a tall story

explanation.surface: Cabins aren't usually found aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the crossword convention for being inside the steamship abbreviation; a tall story is an unlikely one. 'are' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalls are partitioned spaces, as for horses in a stable or for traders at a market.
